current.text: Detroit traded for him in the offseason.
He is projected as Detroit's sixth man and backup shooter. Ron Holland, Paul Reed and Daniss Jenkins are behind him in the bench rotation.
Duncan Robinson is in the projected starting five.
Joe is seen as the most likely player to take Robinson's starting spot.
Detroit used a deep 12 to 13 player rotation last season, which limited everyone's minutes.
Experts do not trust coach JB Bickerstaff's comments about minutes.
He is ranked outside the top 250 for fantasy. His value is as a three-point streamer, not as a draft pick.
For a season ending March 28, Detroit plays 4, 3 and 4 games in the fantasy playoff weeks. The team has 15 back-to-backs.
No rest risks are expected for Detroit players on back-to-backs.

durable.text: He is an elite three-point shooter with low usage who adds little else.
His value comes from threes, few turnovers and a good FT% on low volume. His rebounds, assists, steals and blocks are below the top 250 pool.
He can get hot from three in the regular season. His shooting fell off in the second half of last season.
He creates some turnovers on defense. His overall defense kept him out of OKC's rotation in the last two playoff runs.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD (Yahoo rank 255, ESPN rank 190), and only 144 players get drafted, so do not draft him. He is a waiver streamer for threes. He projects about 2.5 3PM with very few turnovers on roughly 21 minutes, but he gives little in REB, AST, STL and BLK. Early in the season, check whether he takes Duncan Robinson's starting spot or gets more than 21 minutes, since that would make him worth holding in 3PM-heavy builds.
